status: acceptance requirements, not completed journey proofs

backend.evidence: Aurora providers, policy guards, local database contracts and verified local collaboration exist.
backend.gap: Unapplied work-document/comment migrations; current cloud identity → write → agent completion → durable reload has not been established.
backend.gate: A real user creates work, another reviews it, an agent writes its result once, and the result survives a service replacement with correct access and audit history.

journeys.name: Find and complete assigned work
journeys.trigger: A person starts their working day or follows an assignment notification.
steps: See assignments, due dates and blockers without opening an operations tool.
Open the initiative and work item; read its owner, acceptance criteria, evidence and dependencies.
Add the required work or evidence, submit for review, and see who is responsible next.
Return from the notification or reload and see the same persisted state.
journeys.outcome: The item advances with an owner and recorded evidence; the initiative reflects its actual state.
journeys.recovery: Empty assignments explain how work is assigned; failed saves retain edits; stale edits show a conflict; inaccessible deep links offer a useful return path.
journeys.authority: Membership and work-write authority are checked at API and realtime boundaries, including after revocation.
journeys.proof: Real Aurora write/read after process replacement; concurrent edit rejection; notification navigation; private initiative denial.

journeys.name: Plan an initiative and unblock a decision
journeys.trigger: A delivery milestone is blocked by a decision.
steps: State outcome, accountable owner, milestone and success criteria.
Create or attach the blocking decision and supporting documents.
Send the decision to an authorized reviewer; expose the reviewer and waiting state on the initiative.
Reviewer records rationale; the dependency and initiative update together.
journeys.outcome: Everyone can explain what changed, who decided and which work is now unblocked.
journeys.recovery: Missing approver, rejected decision and changed evidence each show the next action; duplicate submissions create one decision.
journeys.authority: An owner cannot silently act as a different reviewer; unauthorized users cannot access attached evidence.
journeys.proof: Cross-record consistency, durable rationale, duplicate-submit protection and permission-aware evidence links.

journeys.name: Run automation and recover a failure
journeys.trigger: Approved work is ready to execute, or a run has failed.
steps: Choose eligible work and a versioned procedure; show prerequisites and execution scope.
Launch once and see queued, running and waiting-for-review states.
Inspect output and evidence; accept or reject proposed changes within authority.
If execution fails, distinguish retryable failure from work needing correction and resume deliberately.
journeys.outcome: The run has an attributable result or an actionable terminal failure; proposed changes are not silently applied.
journeys.recovery: Timeout, lost worker, budget limit, approval denial and duplicate callbacks all have explicit outcomes.
journeys.authority: Run, approve and apply permissions remain separate; budget and tool authority are enforced server-side.
journeys.proof: Real AgentCore dispatch/callback, restart recovery, idempotent completion, bounded retry and cost attribution.

journeys.name: Find knowledge or an expert and act on it
journeys.trigger: A person needs evidence or help to complete work.
steps: Ask a task-specific question or search in the current initiative.
Read an answer with source freshness and accessible citations.
Open the source or contact the person with the work context attached.
Return to the item and record the resulting decision or evidence.
journeys.outcome: The answer leads to a verifiable source and useful work, rather than an isolated chat response.
journeys.recovery: No result, stale index, unavailable model and inaccessible citation are distinct; never fabricate a source.
journeys.authority: Search results, snippets, citations and follow-up conversations obey current grants.
journeys.proof: Fresh live ingestion → indexed retrieval → authorized citation; grant revocation removes visibility; model failure degrades clearly.

journeys.name: Review delivery and funding
journeys.trigger: A review meeting requires an explanation of progress and spend.
steps: Start with an outcome and compare actual progress to the plan.
Trace cost and risk to the work and runs that caused them.
Inspect relevant expertise or staffing evidence where authorized.
Record an allocation or ownership decision and verify its effect.
journeys.outcome: Leadership can reconcile displayed totals to source records and identify accountable owners.
journeys.recovery: Partial data is marked; absent spend is not shown as zero; rejected allocations preserve the current ledger.
journeys.authority: Sensitive people analytics and budget writes remain restricted even when initiative summaries are readable.
journeys.proof: Real spend reconciliation, budget concurrency, audit attribution and analytics privacy checks.

journeys.name: Improve a reusable procedure or agent
journeys.trigger: A successful run reveals a procedure worth reusing, or an existing procedure needs correction.
steps: Find the asset by the work it performs and inspect its owner and version.
Propose a change with evidence from a run or an explicit requirement.
Review the diff and validate the exact version before accepting it.
Use the accepted asset in a new run and trace the result back to that version.
journeys.outcome: Reusable knowledge improves through an attributable review and affects only intended future runs.
journeys.recovery: A stale base, rejected proposal or failed validation preserves the existing accepted version.
journeys.authority: Read, propose, accept and execute authority are distinct; asset tools do not exceed the caller’s authority.
journeys.proof: Real artifact persistence, version conflict, review attribution and execution of the accepted version; verify each supported asset kind.

journeys.name: Start and recover a working environment
journeys.trigger: Work needs an agent or computer environment.
journeys.entry: /iq/local-compute or authorized Computer Lab → environment → session
steps: See availability, permitted tools, repository and expected cost before starting.
Start once and wait for a positive ready state.
Connect to the session and keep its work linked to the initiating task.
Reconnect after interruption, preserve output, then stop the environment and confirm resources are released.
journeys.outcome: The environment is usable, scoped to the right work and does not continue billing unnoticed.
journeys.recovery: Capacity exhaustion, failed bootstrap, lost connection and expired credentials have explicit recovery paths.
journeys.authority: Environment access, repository credentials and tool execution use scoped authority; secrets are never rendered.
journeys.proof: Actual environment lifecycle, remote session reconnect, persistent output, cost limits and verified shutdown.

backend.status: Aurora branch implemented; live execution unproven
backend.evidence: 61 sealed local journeys; transactional admission/completion and stopped-run guards are implemented.
backend.gap: The local browser uses mock Aurora and AgentCore. Database/agent integration and deployment migrations still require a live proof.
backend.gate: Import real evidence, score through the actual runtime, approve the result, reproduce the report, restart services and verify the same provenance.

journeys.name: Bring a team and evidence into assessment
journeys.trigger: A team is ready for its first assessment.
steps: Identify the team, lead and assessment scope.
Upload or connect evidence; distinguish parsing, validation and committed submission.
Resolve missing fields and inspect the import summary before committing.
See the committed evidence attached to the correct team and assessment cycle.
journeys.outcome: One durable submission has clear ownership, source and version.
journeys.recovery: Parse errors retain source context; expired staging asks for re-upload; duplicate commits do not duplicate evidence.
journeys.authority: Only authorized assessors import for the selected team; storage access matches document authority.
journeys.proof: Real upload/storage, parse/commit lifecycle, duplicate submission, staging expiry and durable evidence access.

journeys.name: Verify a claim against evidence
journeys.trigger: An assessment has claims awaiting verification.
steps: See claimed level, verified level and exact missing evidence together.
Open cited evidence and record the reasoning for a score.
Create a follow-up with an owner when evidence is insufficient.
Save and verify that team status and the report agree.
journeys.outcome: A score is attributable, evidence-backed and consistent across team and report views.
journeys.recovery: Concurrent assessor changes are reconciled; removed evidence is flagged; a failed save preserves the draft.
journeys.authority: Score writes use current role and team access; evidence does not leak through a citation.
journeys.proof: Aurora transaction/concurrency, provenance stamps and report rollup consistency using real records.

journeys.name: Resolve feedback and exceptions
journeys.trigger: A contributor requests clarification or a not-applicable exception.
steps: Open a queue ordered by decisions awaiting the current reviewer.
Read the claim, supporting reason and previous conversation in context.
Approve, reject or request more information with a rationale.
Notify the submitter and update the criterion and rollup without losing the original claim.
journeys.outcome: The requester knows the decision, the reason and their next step.
journeys.recovery: No eligible approver, duplicate decision and changed source evidence remain visible and recoverable.
journeys.authority: Exception approval is separate from submitting the request; cross-team reads are enforced.
journeys.proof: Concurrent decision tests on real persistence; actor attribution and correct notification recipient.

journeys.name: Run an evidence assistant and recover
journeys.trigger: Evidence needs extraction or a draft assessment.
steps: Select an eligible command and committed source.
Launch and inspect queue, running and completion states.
Compare generated suggestions to source evidence before accepting them.
Stop, retry or correct failed work with a clear explanation of remote execution state.
journeys.outcome: An attributable suggestion or failure is persisted once and never silently overwrites a stopped run.
journeys.recovery: Missing material fails before reservation; late callbacks after stop cannot write scores; service replacement does not lose accepted inputs.
journeys.authority: The launch actor comes from the session; tool/runtime permissions and team scope are server-enforced.
journeys.proof: Actual Aurora + AgentCore together, callback authentication, late completion, crash recovery and budget limits.

journeys.name: Publish and revisit an assessment report
journeys.trigger: A review cycle is ready for an accountable result.
steps: Review unresolved claims and exceptions before publication.
Trace report summaries to scored dimensions and evidence.
Publish a named version and share it with an authorized reader.
Reopen the published version after later edits and distinguish it from current working scores.
journeys.outcome: A reader can understand the result, its date and supporting evidence.
journeys.recovery: A report with missing evidence is explicit; publication failure cannot create a misleading success state.
journeys.authority: Publication, draft access and shared links follow report/document permissions.
journeys.proof: Durable version semantics, stable evidence links, permission-aware sharing and publish/reload round trip; verify supported publication behavior before promising it.

backend.status: Real local media proven; durable deployment incomplete
backend.evidence: Two-person local calls and record/play/delete flows passed against platform-api and the media stack.
backend.gap: The current gateway reports memory storage. Live-platform rooms, teams, recordings and calls are explicitly missing from the search index without a caller token.
backend.gate: Use durable chat and production media storage; prove access, reconnect, restart persistence, recording lifecycle and live search across two real users.

journeys.name: Discover and join an ongoing room
journeys.trigger: A person wants to join colleagues without arranging a new call.
journeys.entry: /social/rooms or the host workspace Communication → Rooms
steps: See a room directory in the main area with purpose, access and occupancy.
Filter by active rooms or search a name; open details without joining unexpectedly.
Preview microphone/camera and join with an explicit action.
Keep room context visible during the call; leave and return to the directory.
journeys.outcome: The user understands where they joined, who can hear them and how to leave.
journeys.recovery: No rooms gives a role-appropriate next step; denied media has recovery instructions; stale occupancy never guarantees an empty call; private rooms do not leak.
journeys.authority: Only creators/members see private rooms; room creation is offered only with the right capability.
journeys.proof: Real token-scoped listing, join denial, media permissions, reconnect, leave, narrow-screen navigation and two-person call.

journeys.name: Start and continue a conversation
journeys.trigger: A person needs an answer from a colleague or group.
steps: Find the person or channel by name and see why it is relevant.
Send a message with a clear pending, sent or failed state.
Follow replies, mentions and attached work without losing the conversation.
Reload or change device and return to the same history and unread position.
journeys.outcome: The message reaches the intended audience and the sender can verify its state.
journeys.recovery: Offline sends, duplicate retries, expired sessions and deleted messages have explicit outcomes.
journeys.authority: Membership is checked on reads, writes, subscriptions, mentions and attachments.
journeys.proof: Durable chat history and read cursor, reconnect replay/deduplication and revocation during an open socket.

journeys.name: Create and manage a team or room
journeys.trigger: A group needs a persistent place to collaborate.
steps: Name the purpose and choose public/private access.
Add permitted members and explain who can invite others.
Open the resulting room/channel and verify member access.
Change membership or archive the space with clear consequences.
journeys.outcome: The intended people can find the space; removed people lose access promptly.
journeys.recovery: Name conflicts, partial member updates and interrupted creation are recoverable; ordinary participants get an honest request path.
journeys.authority: Creation, invitations, membership changes and archive actions are gated at both BFF and platform.
journeys.proof: Real platform persistence, atomic/idempotent creation, membership race, archive/reload and immediate access revocation.

journeys.name: Call someone and handle a missed call
journeys.trigger: A conversation needs a live discussion.
steps: Start a call from the existing conversation with the recipient visible.
The recipient accepts, declines or misses the ring.
Both parties can leave without losing the DM or call state.
A missed/cancelled unanswered call has a consistent log and a clear return-call action.
journeys.outcome: Call state and history agree for both people.
journeys.recovery: Caller cancellation, reconnect, busy recipient and permission denial do not leave a stuck call.
journeys.authority: Only authorized conversation members can join, read call history or subscribe to call events.
journeys.proof: Two-person cross-browser proof, bounded ring timeout, duplicate signals and service reconnect.

journeys.name: Record, find and manage a meeting recording
journeys.trigger: A meeting outcome needs to be revisited.
steps: Start recording with visible status and applicable authority.
See processing or failure after the call; play when media is ready.
Find by meeting context, open the transcript and return to the source conversation.
An authorized manager deletes the recording and observes consistent removal.
journeys.outcome: Playback and transcript match the meeting; deletion is reflected in every supported view.
journeys.recovery: Missing media, failed processing and expired links have recoverable states; deletion cannot leave a falsely playable item.
journeys.authority: Recording ownership, playback URLs, transcript reads and deletion use current permissions.
journeys.proof: Durable media/object lifecycle, signed URL expiry, transcript processing, delete consistency and real-platform search indexing.

backend.status: Real providers exist; execution matrix needs proof
backend.evidence: The run projection reads existing real providers and reports unavailable sources. Definitions/configuration have Aurora branches.
backend.gap: A unified ledger is not proof that each run kind, queue, approval and recovery path works against actual infrastructure.
backend.gate: For each supported run kind: version → dry run → separate approval → execute → artifact → cancel/retry, with worker loss and duplicate delivery.

journeys.name: Triage a failed or stuck run
journeys.trigger: An alert or attention queue identifies a failure.
steps: See cause, affected work, owner and the most recent successful step.
Open logs and artifacts in the same run context.
Choose an allowed retry, resume, cancel or escalation with its effects stated.
Observe a new attributable attempt and a reliable terminal state.
journeys.outcome: The operator resolves the failure without duplicating side effects.
journeys.recovery: Unavailable source, worker loss, poison message and exhausted retry budget are distinguishable.
journeys.authority: Operators can recover allowed work but cannot bypass authoring or approval policy.
journeys.proof: Real queue delivery, leases, dead-letter behavior, idempotency and recovery after worker replacement.

journeys.name: Author and validate a pipeline definition
journeys.trigger: A repeatable process needs a change.
steps: Choose the definition, owner, input contract and allowed tools.
Edit a draft and compare it to the published version.
Run a bounded dry run and inspect outputs and failures.
Submit the exact tested version for approval.
journeys.outcome: A reproducible, versioned definition is ready for a different person to approve.
journeys.recovery: Invalid configuration, changed base version and failing dry runs block promotion with useful feedback.
journeys.authority: Authoring permission does not imply approval or production execution authority.
journeys.proof: Durable versions, input validation, real dry-run records and promotion bound to the tested version.

journeys.name: Review and approve a promotion
journeys.trigger: A tested definition awaits a decision.
steps: See the version diff, risk, owner and dry-run evidence.
Verify that prerequisites still apply.
Approve or reject with a rationale and see the resulting execution eligibility.
Return later and identify exactly which version was approved.
journeys.outcome: One authorized decision applies to the intended version and is auditable.
journeys.recovery: Stale version, duplicate decision and missing evidence prevent silent promotion.
journeys.authority: Separation of duties and required approver roles are checked at decision time.
journeys.proof: Concurrent approval, stale evidence/version rejection, durable decision and permission revocation.

journeys.name: Launch and follow an approved run
journeys.trigger: An approved process is ready to execute.
steps: Provide validated inputs and inspect scope, cost limit and version.
Launch once; show queue position/state and owner.
Follow steps, approvals, logs and artifacts.
Open the final output in its owning workspace.
journeys.outcome: The run completes once with traceable inputs, outputs, cost and actor.
journeys.recovery: Transport timeout, duplicate launch and partial provider outage do not fabricate success.
journeys.authority: Launch authority, artifact visibility and tool access remain scoped to the source workspace.
journeys.proof: Real runner/queue/artifact store for each producer kind, restart durability and cross-workspace access.

journeys.name: Operate queues and automation policy
journeys.trigger: Capacity, failure volume or policy requires intervention.
steps: Inspect backlog, active workers and dead-letter causes.
Pause or adjust an allowed source without losing queued work.
Change policy with its scope and effective time visible.
Verify recovery and review the change audit.
journeys.outcome: Operations changes have bounded effects and do not lose or replay work unexpectedly.
journeys.recovery: Disconnected worker, unavailable metrics and failed policy save remain visible.
journeys.authority: Administrative policy writes are separate from ordinary run access; secrets never appear in client payloads.
journeys.proof: Backpressure/load test at an agreed target, worker rolling restart, policy durability and useful alerts.

backend.evidence: Native PostgreSQL contracts passed 11/11 on October 19 for concurrency, decisions, grant changes and recovery.
backend.gap: providers/access.ts still throws 503 whenever mock Aurora is off. Applying a schema alone will not connect these provider functions to durable storage.
backend.gate: Wire the real provider and apply the migration; then request → separate approval → actual entitlement → session enforcement → expiry/revoke → audit, through the running service.

journeys.name: Understand and request access
journeys.trigger: A person cannot do their work or needs time-limited access.
steps: See existing access and find a requestable role or resource in plain language.
Explain purpose, beneficiary and duration; see conflicts before submission.
Submit once and see the current reviewer and expected next step.
Follow requests for information without submitting a duplicate request.
journeys.outcome: A durable request identifies what is requested, for whom, why and for how long.
journeys.recovery: Existing entitlement, duplicate request, policy conflict and no eligible reviewer get specific recovery paths.
journeys.authority: Requesters act for themselves; requesting for others follows explicit role and manager authority.
journeys.proof: Real provider request round trip, policy evaluation, duplicate submit and restart persistence.

journeys.name: Decide a request with separation of duties
journeys.trigger: A request enters the approver inbox.
steps: See the beneficiary, resource, duration and business reason.
Review policy conflicts and the complete decision chain.
Approve, reject or request information with a reason.
See whether another step remains or provisioning has begun.
journeys.outcome: The decision is attributable and cannot be mistaken for completed activation.
journeys.recovery: Self-approval, delegated authority changes, stale requests and concurrent decisions are handled explicitly.
journeys.authority: Eligible approvers are resolved live; the beneficiary cannot approve their own access.
journeys.proof: Running API on real persistence, concurrent decision once, delegation expiry and server-enforced self-approval refusal.

journeys.name: Activate access and verify it works
journeys.trigger: All required decisions are approved.
steps: Show provisioning as a separate state from approval.
Apply the entitlement once and record the effective scope and expiry.
Refresh session authority and open the destination workspace.
Verify the granted action works and unrelated actions remain denied.
journeys.outcome: Approved access becomes a usable, bounded entitlement with audit evidence.
journeys.recovery: Provisioning failure has retry/escalation; a worker crash resumes without duplicate grants; stale sessions refresh safely.
journeys.authority: Grant changes use current authorized decisions and preserve unrelated entitlements.
journeys.proof: Real grant writer, idempotent provisioning, crash recovery, Cognito/session integration and end-to-end permission proof.

journeys.name: Expire or revoke access everywhere
journeys.trigger: Access reaches its end date or must be removed.
steps: Identify the exact entitlement and any dependent access.
Revoke once or allow the expiry worker to act.
Invalidate active authority and observe refusal on the next protected action.
Preserve the original approval and the revocation reason in audit history.
journeys.outcome: The removed privilege cannot be used through an old session, API call, socket or shared link.
journeys.recovery: Concurrent renewal/revoke, disconnected clients and delayed sweeps produce an explicit final state.
journeys.authority: Only authorized revokers act; removing one grant preserves unrelated roles.
journeys.proof: Real expiry scheduler, live session/socket revocation, concurrent grant edits and durable audit.

journeys.name: Review entitlements and maintain policy
journeys.trigger: A periodic review or policy change is due.
steps: See current beneficiaries, accountable reviewers and deadlines.
Review evidence and attest, revoke or request clarification.
Adjust policy or delegation with the effective scope visible.
Reconcile review outcomes to actual entitlements and export an authorized audit view.
journeys.outcome: The organization can explain who has access and why, with review actions actually applied.
journeys.recovery: Missing manager, expired delegate, incomplete review and failed revoke remain outstanding.
journeys.authority: Policy editing, review decisions and audit visibility have separate authority; delegation never enables self-approval.
journeys.proof: Real review persistence, scheduled escalation, delegation boundaries and reconciliation against live grants.

sharedJourneys.name: Create, review and share a document
sharedJourneys.trigger: Work needs a durable document, diagram or report.
sharedJourneys.entry: Owning work record → documents → draft, review and published version
steps: Create or attach the document with its work context intact.
Edit with another authorized contributor and inspect version history.
Request and record review before publishing where the workflow requires it.
Share a stable link, revisit a prior version and verify that permissions follow the document.
sharedJourneys.outcome: The document has an accountable version, supported collaborative behavior and a reliable link back to its work.
sharedJourneys.recovery: Concurrent edits, offline changes, deleted attachments and rejected review do not silently lose content.
sharedJourneys.authority: Each document/deck type must use its actual read, edit, review and publish permissions; do not infer parity from a shared editor.
sharedJourneys.proof: Real content/object stores, collaborative reconnect, comment migration, version restoration and cross-role share-link checks for each supported content type.

sharedJourneys.name: Connect a source and keep knowledge current
sharedJourneys.trigger: An organization adds or changes a source of truth.
sharedJourneys.entry: Knowledge administration → source → ingestion → search and cited answer
steps: Connect the supported source with scoped credentials and inspect intended data access.
Run ingestion and expose validation, progress and errors.
Find a newly ingested item and open its exact source from search.
Update or remove the source item and verify that index, citations and access converge.
sharedJourneys.outcome: Knowledge is current, traceable and subject to the source’s access rules.
sharedJourneys.recovery: Expired credentials, rate limits, partial imports and deleted sources show actionable states and safe resumable progress.
sharedJourneys.authority: Connector credentials and document ACLs stay scoped; index results cannot broaden source authority.
sharedJourneys.proof: Live connector ingestion, actual storage/index/model path, ACL propagation, freshness/deletion convergence and credential rotation.

sharedJourneys.name: First sign-in and workspace selection
sharedJourneys.trigger: An administrator provisions a user through the supported identity system.
steps: Complete real SSO and see only granted workspaces.
Choose a workspace and understand its purpose and next action.
Follow an invited deep link without losing intended context.
Sign out and verify that expired sessions return safely to sign-in.
sharedJourneys.outcome: A new user reaches useful work without fixture identities or developer setup.
sharedJourneys.recovery: No grants, disabled account, expired invitation and identity-provider failure each have a clear explanation.
sharedJourneys.authority: Claims are server-validated; workspace choice cannot create grants.
sharedJourneys.proof: Actual identity-provider provisioning, callback, logout, expiry and deprovisioning; picker-mode proof is insufficient.

sharedJourneys.name: Private work remains private across every surface
sharedJourneys.trigger: A private record is created or a user loses access.
sharedJourneys.entry: Direct URL, search, notifications, chat, files and realtime
steps: Create an allowed private record and share only with the intended reader.
Attempt access from a different role and workspace.
Remove the allowed reader while their page/socket is open.
Recheck links, previews, files, cached search and subscriptions.
sharedJourneys.outcome: No protected content leaks through a secondary surface.
sharedJourneys.recovery: Stale caches and reconnects fail closed while preserving useful user-facing explanations.
sharedJourneys.authority: Separate product-workspace isolation from separate client-organization isolation.
sharedJourneys.proof: Cross-user/product tests plus an agreed client deployment isolation model; two organizations if shared SaaS is intended.

sharedJourneys.name: Recover from interruption without losing work
sharedJourneys.trigger: The network, browser, worker or service is interrupted.
steps: Create a draft or start a real operation.
Interrupt at a known stage and restore connectivity.
See which data was saved, pending or failed.
Retry without duplicate side effects and recover the same record.
sharedJourneys.outcome: The user can explain the final state and resume safely.
sharedJourneys.recovery: Conflicts, timeouts and partial success never become silent data loss.
sharedJourneys.authority: Resumption revalidates current grants and operation ownership.
sharedJourneys.proof: Browser offline/reconnect, BFF replacement, worker crash, database transient failure and duplicate delivery.

sharedJourneys.name: Operate and restore a client environment
sharedJourneys.trigger: A deployment, incident or restore is required.
steps: Deploy the exact schema and service versions with preflight checks.
Observe dependency readiness, errors, latency and job age.
Rollback or recover a failed deployment without corrupting data.
Restore a backup and verify selected business journeys.
sharedJourneys.outcome: The service has an owned recovery path and measurable operating limits.
sharedJourneys.recovery: Migration failure, partial provider outage and missing secrets cause bounded failure and actionable alerts.
sharedJourneys.authority: Operator access is restricted and audited; client data and secrets stay out of logs.
sharedJourneys.proof: Staging deploy/rollback, backup restore, secret rotation, target-load test and alert exercise with explicit recovery objectives.
